L104: **Coordinated disease disjunction.** A contiguous span in which a coordinator (e.g., “or,” “and,” “and/or,” a slash, “nor”) joins two or more disease terms is one **Composite Mention** when a conjunct depends on the shared head or modifier for its disease identity. This includes elliptical forms in which the head noun appears only once after the last conjunct (e.g., “breast or ovarian cancer”; “colorectal, endometrial, and ovarian cancers”). The rule holds in any syntactic slot: prenominal, prepositional complement, or attributive before a non-disease head such as a relational noun phrase (“family history”), a population, a case series, or a study noun.
